claims: Carer Allowance "isn't means-tested against the recipient's own income the way most other payments are"
whys: The site's own navigation (lib/navigation.ts:398) and /carer-allowance/ page title cite a $250,000 Carer Allowance income limit (CARER_ALLOWANCE.incomeLimit). The article contradicts that.

claims: January indexation reflects "movements in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding six months"
whys: Youth Allowance, Austudy, ABSTUDY and Carer Allowance are indexed once a year on 1 January, so the measure should be annual CPI (12 months to the September quarter), not six months. Six-monthly CPI is the pension cycle.
constants: centrelink indexation notes in lib/constants (no constant found)

claims: Deeming thresholds "are reviewed alongside the Age Pension rate each March and September"
whys: Deeming thresholds are indexed on 1 July. The site's own constants agree: $64,200/$106,200 in March 2026 became $66,800/$110,600 by 20 September 2026, and the Sep 2026 note says "Only the rates changed".

claims: Deeming rates before 20 March 2026 were 0.25% and 2.25% ("ending a multi-year freeze", frozen since May 2020); same claim at lines 8 and 27 and in lib/news.ts:624
whys: My understanding is the freeze ended on 20 September 2025, when rates rose to 0.75% and 2.75%. If so, the March 2026 'before' values and the 'ending a multi-year freeze' framing are wrong. Check against the AGA March 2026 recommendation the page cites.
constants: no DEEMING_MARCH_2026 constant; values hard-coded in the article and lib/news.ts:609,624

claims: The lower deeming rate rose from 0.25% to 1.25% and the upper rate from 2.25% to 3.25%, effective 20 March 2026, after being frozen since May 2020.
whys: Deeming rates were already lifted to 0.75% and 2.75% from 20 September 2025, so a starting point of 0.25%/2.25% in March 2026 looks stale. The March 2026 Age Pension article links to this page and says deeming changed on the same date.
constants: lib/constants/centrelink-income-test.ts DEEMING_SEPTEMBER_2026 (previousLowerRate 0.0125). A March 2026 deeming set with its own previous rates should be held there too.

claims: lifts the point at which a typical worker starts paying net tax to almost $19,985, or up to $24,985
whys: At the 2027-28 rate of 14%, $18,200 + $250/0.14 = $19,985.71 and $18,200 + $950/0.14 = $24,985.71. That is just over the stated figures, so 'almost' looks inverted. Check against Treasury's wording.
constants: WATO amount and effective tax-free threshold in the tax constants for 2027-28

claims: most health professionals get a rise
whys: Population claim with no figure. Clause J.4.3 (no one goes backwards) shows that some, such as the old Level 4 pay point 4, do not get a rise.
constants: HPSS_OCT_2026 (FWC decision text or a count derived from HPSS translation tables)

claims: 'Most reductions were processed before the end of 2025 ... The ATO has since confirmed processing is complete for all study and training support debts' (key facts line 21: 'Complete as of 2026').
whys: None of the page's three sources is an ATO completion notice (they are Study Assist, Department of Education FAQs and a ministerial release). This needs an ATO or Study Assist source with a date.
